findings.what: Projection validation rejects accepted credential-shaped source identities.
findings.why: The projection rejects a canonical public signal/provenance pair that the existing pipeline can produce. detect.py:676 and :740 recursively redact credential-shaped strings in signal evidence_refs, while provenance retains the structural source_id; test_acquire.py:262 explicitly permits credential-shaped structural source IDs. Requiring evidence_ref.source_id to equal the unredacted provenance source_id therefore makes build_signal_projection fail for accepted source IDs such as ghp_TESTONLY123, violating AC1's public-redacted-contract input and AC5's canonical-reference contract. Validate against the public-redacted representation while retaining table/source-hash binding, and add an end-to-end canonical fixture for an accepted credential-shaped source identity.

findings.what: Lexical search truncates matched_on and collapses query scores.
findings.why: _matched_fields computes every matching public field and then discards all but the last. For the existing Acme fixture both statement and preview.vendor match, but the API reports only preview.vendor and query_score is consequently collapsed to 1 for every nonempty match. This loses the matched_on details required by AC5 and makes the retrieval score incapable of reflecting the matches it purports to count. Return the deterministic full match list and revise the overlapping-field expectation.

findings.what: The combined filter test does not discriminate eight required filters.
findings.why: AC3's only filter test supplies all nine filters together, and signal-alpha is uniquely selected by severity='high' alone. An implementation that ignores detector, group, category, source, table, run, date, and review_state would still pass. Parameterize each filter independently with fixtures or values that change the result set, including a nonmatching review_state.

findings.what: Lexical tests omit three promised detector metadata fields.
findings.why: AC4 and the plan promise lexical search across detector title, description, assumptions, and false-positive metadata, but the matrix exercises only detector.title. A projection that omits the other three consumer-observable metadata fields passes. Add discriminating cases for each promised metadata field; keep the existing statement, warning, and preview cases.

findings.what: The matched_on assertion codifies the production truncation bug.
findings.why: The Acme matched_on assertion encodes the production truncation bug: Acme occurs in both statement and preview.vendor, yet the test requires only preview.vendor. It would reject a correct implementation that reports all deterministic matching fields, weakening AC5 rather than defending it.

findings.what: Stale-projection tests never exercise the required rebuild path.
findings.why: AC6's explicit rebuild path is untested. The matrix proves only that reads reject three changed input families; a builder that works once but refuses to replace an existing stale projection would pass. After each stale rejection, rebuild and prove the changed canonical input is reflected and the new projection is queryable.

findings.what: The score test does not prove separation from editorial attributes.
findings.why: The sole AC7 assertion checks only that query_score is numeric. Setting query_score equal to confidence or another editorial/severity-derived number would pass while violating score separation. Assert a retrieval-defined score across signals with different confidence, severity, and status values; for example, all empty-query scores are zero and equal lexical matches receive equal retrieval scores.

findings.what: The projection module exceeds the module-size standard and mixes responsibilities.
findings.why: The new 566-line module exceeds the authoritative code-standards module-size directive and combines path containment, canonical-input parsing, manifest integrity, DuckDB persistence, and row projection and validation. Split these cohesive responsibilities after the correctness fixes so the trust boundaries remain independently testable.
